subject: Dedicated capacity: performance validation & SLO next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@starlitcommerce.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 16:04:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated capacity: performance validation & SLO next steps

Hi Alex — great speaking earlier. Thanks again for the time and for walking through Starlit's latency and streaming requirements. Quick recap and next steps so we have alignment before we size Dedicated capacity: 

Summary of SLOs you gave on the call:
- P95 latency target: <= 120ms for single-stream text-generation with streaming enabled
- Sustained throughput target: 600 reqs/min (primarily batch small requests, ~1-4 prompts each)
- Peak concurrency target: 40 concurrent streaming sessions
- Max token length: 1,024 tokens (typical 150-400 tokens)
- Availability goal: 99.9% for dedicated pool when in production

What we propose for validation (high-level):
1) Controlled perf test matrix across GPU types (H100-80GB, A100-40GB, and L4-48GB) to compare tail latencies and throughput at target concurrency.
2) Reserved throughput emulation (baseline reservation + 2x burst) to validate autoscaling and fallbacks.
3) Streaming load test with 40 concurrent sessions, varying chunk sizes to ensure real-time tail behavior.
4) KV/prefix caching test using representative prompt set (we'll use a 200-prompt sample you shared).

Deliverables from Redwood:
- Per-GPU perf report (tail P50/P95/P99, measured throughput at SLOs)
- Recommended Dedicated pool sizing and reservation (instances, gpus, expected sustained RPS)
- Test artifacts: scripts, Docker images, and the sizing spreadsheet (attached)

Can you confirm the listed SLO targets above and that we should include H100, A100 and L4 in the matrix? If yes, I'll schedule the validation window next week and copy in our infra lead to lock times.

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-sizing-spreadsheet.xlsx (draft), service-level-summary.pdf

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior AE, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0147
\

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@starlitcommerce.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@starlitcommerce.com
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: performance validation & SLO next steps

Thanks Marissa — that summary looks accurate and covers what we discussed. A few clarifications from our side: 

- P95 <= 120ms is correct for single-stream responses with streaming. For non-streamed responses we can accept slightly higher (P95 <= 200ms).
- Sustained throughput: 600 reqs/min is our baseline for region us-east; we may scale to 900 reqs/min during promos. Please size for 900 as an upper bound.
- Concurrency: 40 concurrent streaming sessions is our primary target; we may test up to 60 for stress.

We definitely want H100 and A100 comparisons. L4 is interesting for cost optimization (lower priority), but include it if easily available. 

Operational notes:
- Procurement will want an estimate of reserved throughput and cost before we start validation. I've looped in procurement for visibility on pricing and contracting timelines.
- We can provide a sample 200-prompt set by EOD today (I'll send a separate email).

Can you include a short section in the deliverable that explains fallback behavior if we hit reserved capacity limits (e.g., model variant fallback, spill to burst pool)? Procurement and infra will want to understand availability guarantees during peak.

Appreciate it — if you can propose the validation slots (PST friendly) we'll confirm.

Best,
Alex
Director, Platform Engineering
Starlit Commerce
alex.johnson@starlitcommerce.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@starlitcommerce.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 11:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: performance validation & SLO next steps

Thanks Alex — great, that helps. Quick updates based on your notes and our internal planning: 

Validation plan (detailed):
- Test matrix: H100-80GB, A100-40GB, L4-48GB (if available). For each GPU type we'll run:
  * Single-stream latency tests (streaming enabled) at 1-40 concurrent sessions
  * Sustained throughput runs at 600/900 reqs/min for 30m windows
  * Stress runs up to 60 concurrent streaming sessions to capture tail behavior
- Reservation sizing: we'll recommend a baseline reservation to comfortably hit 600 reqs/min with P95 <= 120ms on the preferred GPU, plus burst capacity to handle 2x traffic for short periods. We'll produce an explicit instance/gpu count in the sizing spreadsheet attached.
- Fallback behavior: deliverable will include model variant fallback logic (e.g., quantized variant on L4), regional spillover, and graceful degradation strategies (reduced chunk sizes, longer server-side buffering).
- Artifacts: test harness, k6 load scripts, logs, perf plots, and the spreadsheet (attached).

Proposed test windows (PST-friendly):
- Option A: Thu 19 Feb, 09:00-13:00 PST (validation run 1)
- Option B: Fri 20 Feb, 13:00-17:00 PST (validation run 2)

If you want both windows we can split GPU types across them. Procurement: the sizing sheet includes a rough reserved throughput cost estimate to help your team.

I'm attaching the draft spreadsheet now. Once you confirm the windows I'll get our infra team to reserve the nodes.

Thanks,
Marissa

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-sizing-spreadsheet.xlsx

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 13:00:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: performance validation & SLO next steps

Marissa — I can own the infra side for the test windows. Tentative plan:
- Reserve H100 and A100 nodes in us-west for Thu 19 Feb 08:30-13:30 PST; we'll stage L4 if available.
- Set up namespaces to emulate regional traffic (we'll send to us-east endpoints for realism).
- I'll publish a short runbook for the test and ensure logs/metrics go to the shared S3 bucket.

One ask for Alex/procurement: can you confirm whether we should run with encryption-at-rest disabled for faster IO during the test (we'll toggle it back on for production)? Also confirm any IP allowlist entries we should add.

Dylan
Infra Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@starlitcommerce.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@starlitcommerce.com
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 08:45:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: performance validation & SLO next steps

Appreciate the clarity, team. Confirmations: 
- Windows: Thu 19 Feb (Option A) works for us. Please schedule the H100/A100 runs then and L4 if available.
- Encryption: procurement prefers that production parity is maintained. Please keep encryption-at-rest enabled during tests - we can accept the potential small perf delta for realistic numbers.
- IP allowlist: I'll send the CIDR ranges to you in a separate note.
- Procurement: we need the reserved throughput cost estimate in the sizing sheet to start internal approvals. Alex (procurement) will need that by EOD on Mon 16 Feb.

Also: could you add a short section in the perf report that maps observed throughput/latency to estimated monthly cost at three commitment tiers (monthly on-demand, 3mo reserved, 12mo reserved)? That will help our finance team.

Thanks - looking forward to the runs.

Best,
Alex

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@starlitcommerce.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, procurement@starlitcommerce.com
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 09:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: performance validation & SLO next steps

Thanks Alex - noted. We'll keep encryption-at-rest enabled for the runs and add the cost mapping to the perf report (monthly on-demand / 3mo reserved / 12mo reserved).

Action items:
- Marissa: finalize spreadsheet & send updated sizing with costs by Mon 16 Feb (will include DocuSign link for reserved contract estimates).
- Dylan: reserve nodes & publish runbook by Fri 13 Feb.
- Alex: send IP allowlist and 200-prompt sample by EOD Thu 12 Feb.

I'll follow up Monday with the final sizing sheet and confirm the test start time for Thu 19 Feb 09:00 PST.

Thanks all - speak soon.

Marissa
